summary: @servicetitan/datetime-utils ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` script that runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/` into a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes that Bun binary to execute a bundled file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle using string-array rotation and a large hex lookup array; it is not human-readable and executes only under the freshly-downloaded Bun runtime, so Node-based tooling never evaluates the code that runs on install. A datetime utility library has no functional need for an alternate runtime or an opaque 700 KB compiled blob to be executed at install time. The scoped name `@servicetitan/*` is used by ServiceTitan, but this package on the public registry exhibits the alternate-runtime-dropper fingerprint (fetched secondary runtime executing an obfuscated in-tarball payload during `npm install`) rather than a normal library shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
